research_question: Can a supervised false-positive risk head suppress ultra-close MFT to ISRJ cross-talk while preserving at least 90 percent of the frozen P1n recall gain?
failure_target: P3l localized cell-wise FPR failures in ultra_close MFT regimes; P3l identities are excluded from fitting and evaluation

guard.input: frozen 256-D MLCNN latent, shared waveform physics, and six main probabilities
guard.target: frozen P1n false-positive event for the ISRJ output
guard.model: class-balanced HistGradientBoostingClassifier, 200 trees, learning_rate 0.05, max_leaf_nodes 7, l2 1.0
guard.action: set P1n ISRJ probability to zero only when predicted false-positive risk exceeds a selected threshold
guard.selection: training-selection identities only; among thresholds retaining >=90 percent of P1n recall gain and macro-AUPR delta>=-0.005, minimize worst regime-power FPR then veto coverage

next_if_pass: Freeze the guard and repeat two fresh-identity confirmation; do not revisit P3l.
stop_rule: If the guard fails, freeze the latent risk-head branch and retain P1n as Level-3 only; redesign the main backbone with explicit cross-interference supervision on new identities.
